Sheath physics with LaTeXML

Irving Langmuir
Abstract

We revisit the Bohm criterion for a collisionless sheath and derive the floating potential for a two-species plasma in closed form.

1 Introduction

A plasma in contact with a wall forms a sheath a few Debye lengths thick, in which quasineutrality breaks down and ions are accelerated toward the wall by the potential drop that develops there.

2 Theory

Ions must enter the sheath at least at the ion sound speed c, which is the Bohm criterion, and the floating potential follows from balancing the electron and ion fluxes at the wall surface.

2.1 Floating potential

Equating the fluxes gives the classic result for the floating potential of a wall in a hydrogen plasma, about three times the electron temperature below the plasma potential for the mass ratio considered.

References

  • D. Bohm, The characteristics of electrical discharges in magnetic fields (1949).
  • K.-U. Riemann, J. Phys. D 24, 493 (1991), doi:10.1088/0022-3727/24/4/001.
